Waiting for your signature: conditional CT chest order (below).

response.surgeon: Location: medial right lower zone, small dense nodular focus (F2) on chest radiograph. Size trend: 12 mm on prior to 13 mm on current by supplied measurement, basis unconfirmed. It is indeterminate whether this is a true nodule or new. The report says nothing on whether surgery is possible.
response.family_page:
Your care team will go over this with you.
You had a chest X-ray. It was done as a routine check after your breast cancer treatment.
The X-ray showed a very small spot in the lower part of your right lung. The X-ray cannot tell what the spot is. It could be a normal part of the lung, or it could be something that needs a closer look. The spot was not clearly seen on your last X-ray.
The X-ray also could not show the end of your port tube clearly. A port is a small device under the skin that lets doctors give medicine through a vein.
What your care team recommends next: the radiologist, a doctor who reads X-rays, will look at the original pictures more closely. You may need a CT scan. A CT scan takes more detailed pictures of the inside of your chest. You may also need another X-ray from the side to see your port tube.
Who to call: please call Dr. Okafor's office (medical oncology) with any questions.
